name: EMCOR Group
description: EMCOR is a US electrical and mechanical contractor. It installs the electrical, mechanical (heating, cooling, piping, plumbing, fire protection) and low-voltage systems in new buildings, data centers, chip and pharma plants, hospitals and large commercial projects, and it also sells recurring building-maintenance and facilities services and industrial (plant turnaround and heat-exchanger) services. Most revenue is project work won by competitive bid on fixed-price or similar contracts, recognised as the work progresses, so margin depends on bidding and execution; the 'remaining performance obligations' (contracted work not yet done) were $17.1 billion at June 30, 2026, up from $13.25 billion at year-end 2025. Network and communications work (which includes data centers) rose to 56% of US electrical segment revenue in H1 2026 from 49% a year earlier.

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Industrials' and Sub-Industry 'Construction & Engineering' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30; EMCOR added Sept 22, 2025). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry. SEC SIC code 1731 (Electrical Work) per EDGAR. The box hides that EMCOR's largest customers are data-center and other large-technology builders: network and communications work was 58% of US electrical segment revenue in Q2 2026.

hq.note: 301 Merritt Seven Corporate Park, 6th Floor, Norwalk, CT 06851 (EDGAR business address)

employees.note: About 44,000 people, all in the United States, after the UK operations were sold Dec 1, 2025 (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: US mechanical construction and facilities services
businessLines.how: Building owners and general contractors pay per project, mostly under competitive-bid fixed-price or guaranteed-maximum-price contracts recognised as work progresses; profit is the margin over labour, materials and subcontract costs, so bid accuracy and execution matter, and high-tech and data-center demand has lifted volume.
businessLines.description: Mechanical, HVAC, piping, plumbing, fire protection and related construction and services for new and existing facilities.

businessLines.name: US electrical construction and facilities services
businessLines.how: Same fixed-price and bid-based project model as mechanical; the segment's growth is concentrated in data centers and other network and communications construction, where clients pay per project as work progresses.
businessLines.description: Electrical power, lighting, low-voltage and communications systems installed in new and existing facilities.

businessLines.name: US building services
businessLines.how: Building owners and government sites pay recurring fees under service and maintenance contracts and for repair and project work; margins are lower (about 6%) but revenue is steadier than new construction.
businessLines.description: Recurring mechanical services, commercial and government site-based facilities services and other maintenance for buildings.

businessLines.name: US industrial services
businessLines.how: Plant owners pay for turnaround and maintenance work (demand varies with turnaround projects, which the 10-K cites as the reason for the FY2025 dip) and for heat exchangers built to order; margins are thin (about 2% in FY2025).
businessLines.description: Turnaround and maintenance services for industrial plants and heat-exchanger manufacturing.

businessLines.name: United Kingdom building services (sold December 1, 2025)
businessLines.how: Service contracts and project work for UK buildings; no longer part of the company.
businessLines.description: UK facilities services, sold on Dec 1, 2025.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $21.5M; the sale produced a separate $144.9M gain in FY2025 consolidated operating income
